text: The last lesson covered what Helm is and the problems it solves. This one builds the real thing — a chart for Northbridge's product-catalog service, from helm create through a finished templates directory you could actually install into a cluster.

helm create scaffolds the standard shape: Chart.yaml holds the chart's name and version — kept separate from appVersion, the version of product-catalog itself — values.yaml holds the configurable defaults, and templates holds the actual manifests, written with double-curly-brace placeholders instead of hardcoded values.

A placeholder like Values.replicaCount pulls straight from values.yaml. Release.Name and Chart.Name are built in automatically — Release.Name is whatever name you give helm install — so the same template produces correctly named, uniquely configured resources for every release, without editing the template itself.

Before anything touches the cluster, helm lint checks the chart's structure and syntax on its own, with no install involved. helm template goes further and renders the actual YAML Helm would apply, locally, so you can read the real output and catch a typo in a template expression before it becomes a broken Deployment in production.
That's a working, validated chart for product-catalog, ready for a real install. Next lesson: what to actually do when this chart's Pods don't come up clean — troubleshooting Pods and nodes.
